lens: Cost and feasibility (NS13). I recomputed every proposal's per-ayah cost from the recorded ledgers, using one calibrated token formula and one set of reconciled rates. claude -p: input billed as 1-hour write $8/M, output $20/M, cache read $0.20/M; this reconciles exactly on all 28 v15 calls. Batch (claude-api skill): 50% off every token including cache, so $2 input / $10 output / $0.10 cache read / $4 for a 1-hour write; single-shot, no tool loop, caching best-effort. I then checked what breaks at long-surah scale and on the CLI (64K per-response cap, no cross-call prefix reuse). Scripts and outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-502/-Volumes-OZTURK--projects-prose-generation/9b253717-be1d-4238-a42b-f4b098b1d894/scratchpad/phase2/X-cost-critic/.

objections.objection: The output assumption (20–45k including thinking) contradicts D's own confound table. Fed calls with memory permission, which is exactly D's synthesis condition, produced a median of 50.6k output tokens (32.7k thinking, max 76k, n=16), against 22.2k for the no-permission arms whose shape D borrows. So D's CLI cost per synthesis call is about $0.9 (1:6) to $1.9 (4:34, 5:6), not $0.5–1.7. Production is about $0.43–0.77 per call and about $0.59 per ayah across the whole Quran, not $0.2–0.7.
objections.evidence: c03_output_shape.py → out_c03_output_shape.txt (FED-PERM out median 50,556, thinking 32,722; FED-NOPERM 22,218 / 13,664); c07_cost_model.py → out_c07_cost_model.txt ('D KA packet' rows: CLI P 0.52–1.60 vs R 0.92–1.90; Batch R 0.43–0.77; whole Quran R $3,658)

objections.objection: Long ayat under the no-caps rule go past the CLI's 64K per-response cap. Cold-arm output grows by about 764 tokens per ayah word; 4:34 cold already reached 60,210. For 2:282-class ayat (D built 2:282 at 80.9k input) the call needs a continuation turn on the CLI, which v11 recorded at about $0.5 of re-billed input each, or it has to go through the API.
objections.evidence: c03 fit out ≈ 16.5k + 764×words (extrapolated 2:282 ≈ 114k, 16 ayat > 64K; this is an inference from 3 long data points); v13/HANDOFF.md:151 'The CLI caps one response at 64K output tokens whatever CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS says; thinking counts'; v11/REVIEW.md:277–278 second turns ≈ $0.5 each

objections.objection: The validation budgets are low. V1 (48 calls, '≈$36') comes to about $50–65 at the recorded permitted-and-fed output. V2 appends a 150–400k bulk package, so its 400k-input calls cost about $3.6–4.1 each, not $2.3. The probe assumes 1.5–3k output per root at effort low, which is too little for roots with 10–40 branches; a plausible total is $30–70, and the effort-high pilot $6–18 rather than $3–9.
objections.evidence: c07 rates; metrics.tsv package arm (w10-opus) costs up to $3.69 at 318–414k input; the dictionary averages about 6.9 branches per root (11,773 branches / 1,708 entries)

objections.objection: 'Whole surah as a cached prefix' saves nothing in tests. The recorded claude -p calls show no cross-call reuse of user content (only the CLI's own 531–1,459-token prefix was read from cache), so every test call pays the surah text at $8/M; for S3/S4 that is $0.27–0.30. D's CLI figures do include the surah in billed input, so its own test numbers are internally consistent. The saving exists only through the Batch/API, where it is best-effort.
objections.evidence: v15 out*/**/*.raw.json: write calls cache_read_input_tokens 531/1,459 constant; v15 prompts diverge at char 73, so cross-call prefix reuse was never exercised (inline check; out_c09_rate_reconcile.txt)

cross_cutting: Output (thinking), not input, drives cost: 49–94% of recorded spend. Every proposal borrows its output shape from the v9 arms that ran without permission (22k), then grants memory. Recorded permitted, fed calls produce 50.6k (thinking 32.7k, 2.4× higher). Re-price every permitted synthesis call at 40–60k output: that raises the per-ayah estimates by 40–70% (c03, c07).

The CLI caps one response at 64K output, thinking included (v13 HANDOFF:151). Under the no-caps rule, cold-arm output grows by about 764 tokens per ayah word, and 4:34 is already at 60k. The longest ayat (2:282, 2:102, 24:31, 73:20; 16 over 64K by extrapolation), surah commentaries of long surahs, and long S1/S-reading windows need the API (128K) or continuation turns at about $0.5 each (v11 REVIEW:277). Plan those on the API from the first test.

The CLI shows no cross-call prefix reuse (cache reads of 531–1,459 tokens), and 48% of v15 spend was 1-hour writes. Every 'cached surah prefix' saving (A, B, D) exists only through the API/Batch. Tests pay full input at $8/M, so a sync API call at $4/M input is cheaper than the CLI for input-heavy calls (A's S1 windows, B's R_lex).

Batch is single-shot: no tool loop and no same-session turns, with caching best-effort within a batch (claude-api skill §2.5). Four designs test with Read or pull access (A's lookup, C1/C2 pull.json, D pull paths, B's optional pull), and B relies on a same-session challenge. What V1 measures would not be what production runs. The Batch runner every production figure depends on was designed in v8, v11 and v13 and never built.

Long-surah scale: 83.9% of lines are in surahs over 40 ayat. The 24 surahs without HFT hold about 3,113 ayat (half the Quran), all long, none in v5. Pericopes average 16.8 ayat, not 7–10. S2 has a 61k-token review and 60k tokens of text. A single surah-commentary call cannot read S2's ayah commentaries (1.6–1.8M tokens uncapped), so any surah layer must be pericope-then-surah, which is a hidden stage and a new selection point.

Token estimators disagree by up to 40%. Use one calibrated formula (c01: 1.151 per Arabic char, 0.366 per other char, 4,581 intercept; +5% out-of-sample) for every push budget. C1 understates by 25%, C2 by 40%, A overstates by 29%, B and D are within 5%.

The one-time costs are small in dollars and large in wall time. Luna-HFT for Tier 3: $71–143 list-equivalent, 27–37 h at 15 parallel. Whole-Quran loanword cards: about $12, 1.8 h. The D probe: $30–70. C2 construction extraction: under $1. Subscription throughput and rate limits for codex and claude -p are not recorded anywhere, so the wall-time figures are lower bounds.
Validation budgets are about 30–60% low across the board, because each prices its test arms at the cold-arm $0.44 or the dictionary-arm $0.62.
